source_evidence: Proxy statements describe the matters to be voted upon and often disclose information on the company’s executive compensation policies and practices.
answer: A proxy statement helps shareholders understand what they are being asked to vote on. Shareholders may vote to elect board members, cast non-binding votes on executive compensation, approve or reject proposed mergers and acquisitions, or decide other important matters. Proxy statements often also include information about the company’s executive compensation policies and practices.
